spans.s:
hiṅkāra
(‘[the sound] hiṁ’)
------------------------------------------
Vedic sacrifices were the most important aspect of religion in practice in the ancient days. Out of the several acts enjoined in the same, chanting of the sāmans (ṛk-mantras set to मुसिच् according to the Sāmaveda) was also one.
Uttering the word ‘hiṁ’ marked the opening of the सामन् in some sacrifices. It was repeated thrice by the होतृ priest. Sometimes, the उद्गातृ priest did it; but he replaced ‘hiṁ’ by ‘hūm ā’ twice.
When ‘hiṁ’ was repeated thrice followed by ‘bhūr bhuvas suvarom’ it was called ‘abhihiṅkāra’.
